title: Company earnings reports
measures: A listed company's results for the last quarter or year: revenue, profit, earnings per share, cash flow, and often what management expects next (guidance).
whyItMatters: Earnings show how a business is actually doing. A report can change what investors are willing to pay for the shares, and a large company's results can affect its sector or a whole index.
expectations: Analysts publish estimates for revenue and earnings per share. Investors also form views on guidance and on details such as margins, which are harder to summarise in one number.
surprises: Beating or missing the estimates is only part of it. Weak guidance can outweigh a strong quarter, and a small miss can be ignored if the outlook improves. Shares can gap at the next open because reports often come out when the main market is closed.
limits: Good results do not guarantee a rising share price, and poor results do not guarantee a fall. Small companies often have few or no analyst estimates and thin trading, so their moves can be large and unpredictable.
